clue.text: Remarkable theory won't, when revised

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: the ten letters of both words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A thinker's theory, once rewritten, turns out to be remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noteworthy deserves attention, which is a close synonym of remarkable.

clue.text: Verb or adjective, say, as part of speech

blocks.note: surface reading: these look like examples of parts of speech other than the one wanted
setter's reading: the words 'verb' and 'adjective' are themselves names of things, so each is this part of speech

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson listing verbs and adjectives as parts of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is to look at the words 'verb' and 'adjective' as words: each names a thing, so grammatically each is a NOUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun is one of the grammatical word classes, the naming word category.

clue.text: After onset of tears, gives out these?

indicators.note: the onset of something is its beginning, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of tears
to issue something is to give it out

explanation.surface: Once someone starts crying, these are handed round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'These' leans on the whole surface for its meaning: what gets handed out once tears start.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper handkerchiefs are what people offer to someone who has started crying.

clue.text: Reportedly knocking publication that provides present coverage

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than read, so the sound of the word counts, not its spelling

blocks.note: rapping is knocking, and it is pronounced the same as a word for enfolding
a newspaper is a publication

explanation.surface: A newspaper is said to be running a hostile story about the current news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present coverage' looks like up-to-date reporting; here 'present' means gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorated paper is what covers a gift, so it is literally a gift's covering.

clue.text: Spin after moonshine's consumed

blocks.note: moonshine can mean foolish talk, nonsense
's stands for 'has', and has consumed means ate

explanation.surface: Someone's head spins after drinking illicit spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Moonshine suggests bootleg liquor, but here it is its other sense, nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin is to turn round on an axis, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Part of body found in trendy establishment

blocks.note: hip means fashionable
a joint is informal for a bar or restaurant

explanation.surface: A body part turns up in a fashionable bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The ball-and-socket articulation between thigh and pelvis is an anatomical feature.

clue.text: Dishonest activity taking son to front of academic stream

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
the river flowing through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A fraud involving a boy being pushed ahead in a university set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Academic stream' sounds like a teaching set; it is the Cam, the river of Cambridge University.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a swindle or fraudulent scheme, so it is crooked behaviour.

clue.text: Means to exert leverage in constant dispute with lawyers

blocks.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
a row is a quarrel
the Bar is the collective name for barristers

explanation.surface: Someone gains leverage by staying in a long legal dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leverage' reads as bargaining power, but the answer is a literal lever.
explanation.definitionFit: This iron bar with a flattened end is used as a lever to prise things open.

clue.text: Wrongly judging motorway is north of English university town

blocks.note: M as in the M1, a British motorway
taken as written
Reading, a town in Berkshire with a university

explanation.surface: A driver misjudges the motorway north of an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'north of' places the earlier pieces above the next. Reading is pronounced 'redding' as a town.
explanation.definitionFit: A misreading is a mistaken interpretation, so misreading a situation means judging it wrongly.

clue.text: Arrogant newcomer wrongly put over top player

indicators.note: something done wrongly is not in the right order, so the letters are rearranged
to put one thing over another is to cover it, so these letters wrap round the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written before being rearranged
a star is a leading performer

explanation.surface: A cocky newcomer has been wrongly placed above the team's best player.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone who has risen suddenly and behaves presumptuously.

clue.text: Devout accepting empty temple? That's pathetic

indicators.note: emptied of its contents, only the shell of the word is left: its outer letters
accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: pious means religiously devout
first and last letters of temple

explanation.surface: A believer, faced with a deserted temple, finds the sight pathetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Piteous means arousing pity, which is the older sense of pathetic.

clue.text: Part of shoe on dishonest person? It's hard to say

blocks.note: the tongue is the flap under the laces
a twister is a swindler, someone who twists the truth

explanation.surface: Odd questions about a shoe and a cheat, then a shrug: who can say?
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's hard to say' sounds like an admission of uncertainty; read literally it means difficult to pronounce. In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase built to trip up pronunciation is literally difficult to articulate.

clue.text: Finished in one sitting? Novel you reportedly pan wouldn't be

indicators.note: novel means new and unfamiliar, so the letters are made into a fresh arrangement
what is reported is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: the letter U is pronounced like you
the twelve letters of these words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A book reviewer reflects that a novel slated by critics would never be read at a single sitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the book in the picture; it is the anagram signal. The question mark flags that the definition describes a gripping book by its effect.
explanation.definitionFit: A book so compelling the reader cannot stop is typically read in a single session.

clue.text: Mishandled trial never producing material? Not so

indicators.note: something mishandled is botched and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: all ten letters of both words

explanation.surface: A botched court case never yields any useful evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like evidence in the trial; it is the adjective, as in material to the case, then negated by 'Not so'.
explanation.definitionFit: Material here means pertinent, so not material is immaterial, without bearing on the matter.

clue.text: In place of fighting, is standing up

indicators.note: in places the word that follows inside the setting just named

blocks.note: a boxing ring is where bouts are fought
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instead of fighting, someone is standing up for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In place of' reads as 'instead of'; split it, so 'In' is the container signal and 'place of fighting' the boxing arena.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising means getting to one's feet, the action of standing up.

clue.text: Asked, in conclusion, what choir sounds like

indicators.note: in puts the next piece inside the word that follows it
'what choir sounds like' asks for a word pronounced the same as choir

blocks.note: an end is a conclusion
quire, a set of paper sheets, is pronounced like choir

explanation.surface: Someone asked, to wrap up, what the choir sounded like.
explanation.walkthrough: A quire is 24 or 25 sheets of paper, and it is pronounced exactly like choir.
explanation.definitionFit: To enquire is to ask, so its past tense matches asked.

clue.text: Not having weapons around hospital, so not injured

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first word wraps round the next

blocks.note: unarmed means without weapons
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Without weapons near the hospital, so nobody got hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Unharmed means undamaged and unhurt, so free of injury.

clue.text: Taking flight from East, break into song when over limit

indicators.note: over here means covering, so one piece is laid round the next

blocks.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
to break into song is to sing
a cap is an upper limit

explanation.surface: Fleeing from the East, someone bursts into song once past the limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break into' looks like a container signal, but 'break into song' as a whole means sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Escaping means fleeing, and to take flight is to run away.

clue.text: I recant after conversion, for sure

indicators.note: something converted has been changed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: all seven letters

explanation.surface: A convert renounces their old faith, sure of the new one.
explanation.walkthrough: The religious picture of recanting after a conversion disguises the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To be certain is to know without doubt, the same as being sure.

clue.text: Pair holding hands, grasping broken piece of flower

indicators.note: grasping means holding inside, so the pair wraps round the next word

blocks.note: in bridge, South and North are partners, each holding a hand of cards
a broken horse has been tamed

explanation.surface: A couple holding hands clutch a torn bit of a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding hands' paints lovers; in bridge, North and South are a partnership holding two of the four hands.
explanation.definitionFit: The stamen is the pollen-producing male organ, one component part of a bloom.

clue.text: Leading lady or man performing in moving protest

indicators.note: in places the preceding piece inside the word that follows

blocks.note: a march is a protest on the move
a performer is on stage

explanation.surface: A star actor or actress takes part in a protest march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading lady or man' suggests a lead role on stage; it means a queen or king.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch, king or queen, is the foremost person in a nation.

clue.text: Left cold during musical piece that's sweet and soothing

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so these letters go inside the next word

blocks.note: a duet is a piece for two performers
L is the abbreviation for left
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A soothing piece of music left a listener cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Dulcet describes a pleasant, gentle sound, typically a voice or tone.

clue.text: Enterprise Utopians initially put together?

blocks.note: surface reading: a business set up by idealists
setter's reading: the first letters of the two words make the two-letter abbreviation for a political bloc, and 'put together' hints at its second word

explanation.surface: An idealistic business venture founded by dreamers.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of 'Enterprise Utopians' are EU, the abbreviation of this answer, and a body put together is a union.
explanation.definitionFit: The EU is the political and economic association of European states.

clue.text: Spring this year's a little longer than most

definitions.text: this year's a little longer than most

blocks.note: first meaning: to jump

blocks.clueFragment: this year's a little longer than most
blocks.note: second meaning: the kind of year with an extra day in February

explanation.surface: A spring, perhaps, that seems to be lasting longer this year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' tempts as the season; it is the verb meaning jump. A year with 29 February has 366 days.
explanation.definitionFit: To leap is to jump, and a leap year has one extra day added.

clue.text: Article after article with added mass – letter-sorter can handle it

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
a is the other indefinite article
a gram is a unit of mass

explanation.surface: A postal worker who sorts letters handles one item after another, adding weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter-sorter' suggests a mail sorter; here it is a solver rearranging letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearranging a word's letters to make another is exactly the device a letter-shuffler works with.

clue.text: Set small bed beside big lake

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed for a baby
Lake Erie, one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Put a baby's bed down next to a large lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a verb, as in set down; it is the noun, a clique.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive group of people, a social set or clique.

clue.text: Minute can last for eternity?

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that is used

blocks.note: a tin is a can
the final letter of eternity

explanation.surface: Can a single minute last forever?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' reads as the unit of time; it is the adjective (my-NEWT), very small.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute pronounced my-newt means extremely small, the same as tiny.

clue.text: So tried to change fashionable position, on paper

indicators.note: letters made to change are rearranged into a new order

blocks.note: all seven letters before the shuffle
hip means fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone tried to update their fashionable status, at least in theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On paper' sounds like 'in theory'; read literally it means at a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The editor's role is a post held at a newspaper, so it is a job on a paper.
